chapter: Kansas City, Omaha and Lloyd Hunter
title: Lloyd Hunter's band: personnel and rivalry with Nat Towles
summary: He names the members of Hunter's twelve-piece band and explains how it beat Nat Towles's polished band, whose drummer was weak.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: But I stayed with Lloyd for quite a little while. All of -- almost all of '56.
You didn't tell me who was in that band. Do you remember who was in Lloyd Hunter's band, or any of the people?
Jimmy Bythewood was tenor player. A fellow named McKinley was the guitar player. Byron --
Little Byron -- Jimmy Byron was trombone.
Jimmy Cole was the trumpet player.
That was what, a 12-piece band, in sections, wasn't it?
Well, they had a lot of the guys in it.
Oh, a lot of the guys could and did write wrote for it.
And Lloyd did a lot of arranging, too.
He was a good trumpet player.
He didn't get anyplace because he had a good band, and we cut Nat Towles' Cole's band --
And -- because Nat had a good band, and his arranger would sound like Lunceford's, see. And all

the good musicians, but his drummer was weak. And I had gone back to playing drums with Lloyd, see. And Lloyd had gotten another bass player. So his drummer didn't cut the mustard, as they say. He was the weakest guy in the band.
I think he played saxophone, but he would always front the band.

Well, you know what I'm thinking, Gus? I could be wrong on this, but you know I said that Lawson's band in Dallas, that they sent for, and I sent to you they sent for Nat Cole. I wonder if I'm not wrong, and they sent for Nat Towles.
They could have sent for Nat Towles.
Well, wait a minute. Nat Towles' band came out of where?

Yeah, well, what I'm thinking is that Nat Towles came up and fronted the band I'm talking about, Lawson's band, in Dallas. And that became Nat Towles' band. Or maybe it became the second band he had or something.

Well, I don't know about the second -- the second band? See, now, when I met the guys in the band, even Henry Coker was playing trombone in the band, and one of the trumpet players was Walter Duncans, which we all went to school together. We grew up together. And the bass player
was from Dallas, and his mother was a music teacher. Buddy Tate was in the band. Did I tell you?
But he was in that band.
'35 or '36? So, really, it was pretty well a Dallas band, wasn't it?
I had that here a few minutes ago. I'm trying to see all the guys that were in that band.
He could front the band pretty well, couldn't he?
Oh, yes. His band was really sharp, too.
Good arrangements, good musicians, where a large band had -- he had good musicians, but they were kind
Well, if you say they drank a lot, they weren't that -- there wasn't that same band spirit or something.
Well, they'd have the spirit until they would drink so much.
